newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus bank favours Italian cement deal.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus bank favours Italian cement deal.

text.p: The central bank of Cyprus is edging towards approval of plans by the cement company Vassiliko to sell a large bloc of shares to Italy's Italcementi in spite of local opposition.

"I think we would be inconsistent with our policies on encouraging foreign investment if we said 'no' unless there are special reasons -- which do not exist," Central Bank Governor Afxentis Afxentiou told a parliamentary inquiry on Friday.
But tempers flared during the three-hour debate called by opposition MPs on the plans of Vassiliko, one of whose largest shareholders is Cyprus's Greek Orthodox Archbishop Chrysostomos.

The central bank, which vets foreign investment applications, has not yet approved Italcementi plans to raise its stake in Vassiliko to 33 percent from 20 percent. Any recommendations by the parliamentary committee would not be binding for the bank.

The deal has been challenged by Cyprus Cement Company of Stavros Galatariotis. It says that it agreed with Chrysostomos to buy up to 39 percent of Vassiliko shares at 209 cents each, but that the archbishop reneged on the deal at the last minute when Italcementi came along to offer 240 per share.
Galatariotis told the inquiry the sale would put an industry of 'strategic importance' in the hands of foreigners.

"It is inconceivable for Greek Cypriots to discuss the granting of rights to a foreign group with strong connections especially with Turkey, which is at a state of war with us," Galatariotis said, referring to Italcementi interests in Turkey, which has occupied a third of Cyprus since 1974.
Vassiliko chairman Paschalis Paschalides told the MPs: "The control of the company will remain in Greek Cypriot hands...and I have never heard of cement being a strategic material."

Italcementi took a 20 percent stake in Vassiliko, which is controlled by the Hellenic Company Group, in 1990. That agreement gave them a priority option to buy more shares in the company if Vassiliko decided to sell in future.
